title: Ethical Conduct and Humanitarian Health Systems Standards Officer (Re Announced)
description:
About CTG
CTG was established in 2006, almost 20 years ago, in Afghanistan. We currently operate in 35 countries and have approximately 11,500 staff members committed to good!
But do you know who we are? And what do we do?
We provide tailored Human Resources and Staffing Solutions that support critical global initiatives across Humanitarian and Development sectors, and are now strategically foraying into new industries, including Construction, Energy, and IT, with a focus on high-risk regions.
Here’s a list of services we offer:
•Staffing solutions and HR management services
•Monitoring and evaluation
•Fleet management and logistics
•Facilities management
•Sustainability and Communications Advisory
•Election monitoring and observation
•IT professional services
•Medical assistance
Visit www.ctg.org to find out more.

Job Descriptions
Background: Our client in Afghanistan provides technical assistance to the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH) and health sector partners to support the delivery of safe, ethical, and people-centered health services in humanitarian and development settings. In a complex operating environment, upholding ethical conduct and accountability is essential to ensure safe access to health services for communities and dignified, professional service delivery by health workers. All support is provided in line with the Do No Harm principle and our client framework for technical engagement with national health systems.
Purpose of the Position
This consultancy supports efforts to strengthen ethical conduct and professional behavior across the health sector by identifying gaps and opportunities to better align policies, practices, and operational systems with international minimum standards. This is a consultancy position reporting directly to our client under the technical supervision of the designated our client Technical Lead. The consultant will work in close coordination with the MoPH General Directorate of Policy and Planning, while maintaining full our client reporting, accountability, and oversight arrangements.

Job Requirements
Key Responsibilities
The consultant will:
· Identify gaps and opportunities within existing MOPH systems, practices, and operational frameworks to strengthen alignment with international minimum standards in humanitarian and development settings.
· Develop a risk-informed roadmap and prioritized action plan with clear milestones and timelines.
· Provide technical support for the development and application of codes of conduct guiding health workforce behavior.
· Translate international standards into practical tools, SOPs, and operational guidance applicable to health service delivery.
· Design, develop, and deliver contextualized training and sensitization on ethical conduct, codes of conduct, and do no harm principles for health workers, implementing partners, and relevant MoPH counterparts.
· Support the integration of ethical conduct and minimum standards into onboarding processes and routine training systems.
· Provide technical guidance to support program-level implementation of standards at service delivery points.
· Promote community awareness on health rights, dignity, expected staff behavior, and safe access to health services.
· Maintain confidential data systems to track adherence to codes of conduct and minimum standards and produce analytical reports for our client and MoPH technical leadership.
· Strengthen the accessibility, visibility, and appropriate use of confidential reporting and feedback mechanisms.
· Support monitoring, supervision, follow-up, and corrective actions related to ethical conduct and minimum standards by health partners.
· Facilitate coordination with Health Cluster structures and PSEAH inter-agency mechanisms to strengthen alignment of standards, referral pathways, and response approaches.
· Serve as a technical focal point between our client, MoPH technical counterparts, and implementing partners to promote coherence and accountability in safe health service delivery.
Required Qualifications and Experience:
Education
· Bachelor’s degree in law, public health, social sciences, or a related field
Experience
· At least 5 years’ experience in health systems strengthening and application of ethical and minimum standards in humanitarian and development health settings, including experience in Afghanistan
· Proven experience in policy analysis, training, stakeholder engagement, and people-centered risk assessment and mitigation
· Strong understanding of international humanitarian and development standards, medical ethics, and Do No Harm principles
· Commitment to women’s and girls’ right to health
Language
· Fluency in English is a must and working knowledge of Pashto and/or Dari.
Knowledge and Core Competencies
· Strong analytical, coordination, and facilitation skills.
· Ability to work effectively in complex and high-risk environments.
· High standards of integrity, confidentiality, and accountability.
Additional Information
· At no stage of the recruitment process will CTG ask candidates for a fee. This includes during the application stage, interview, assessment and training.
· CTG has a zero tolerance to Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) which is outlined in its Code of Conduct. Protection from SEA is everyone’s responsibility
· CTG encourages all candidates applying for this advertisement to ensure that their candidate profile is up to date with up to date experience / education / contact details, as this will help you being considered further in your application for this role.

title: HMIS Assistant
description:
Job Summary
1. Data Collection, Entry & Management
· Gather, compile, and sort daily and monthly data on service delivery indicators (e.g., Outpatient Department (OPD), antenatal/maternal health, vaccinations, and nutrition metrics).
· Perform accurate data entry into standard databases like the Ministry of Health warehouse and the DHIS2 Platform.
· Maintain and update the HMIS software, ensuring the absolute integrity and security of confidential medical and patient records.
· Manage distribution and stock tracking of standardized HMIS tools, tally sheets, and registers to field locations and health clinics.
2. Data Quality Assurance & Analysis
· Review, clean, and verify health data submitted by clinics prior to processing to prevent double-counting or discrepancies.
· Run regular data quality audits and compile comprehensive data analysis trends to pinpoint service delivery gaps or spikes in local health trends.
· Translate data into charts, dashboards, and statistical summaries for periodic review and evaluation.
3. Monitoring and Field Supervision
· Conduct routine site visits to clinics and outreach locations to observe data entry workflows and check the deployment of tracking logs.
· Review performance indicator tracking systems alongside the broader MEAL team.
· Maintain accountability and feedback tracking tools, logging community and beneficiary recommendations securely.
4. Capacity Building & Coordination
· Provide hands-on, on-the-job training and workshops for healthcare practitioners regarding case definitions, software tools, and reporting timelines.
· Represent the organization during provincial or organizational HMIS subcommittee and coordination meetings.

Job Requirements
Education: Bachelor’s Degree in Public Health, Health Informatics, Information Technology, Statistics, or a medical discipline (Nursing, Midwifery, or Pharmacy).
Experience: Minimum of 1 to 2 years of active experience handling health information data management, monitoring, or medical registers within an NGO, INGO, or public clinic environment.
Technical Skills & Systems: Proven familiarity operating the DHIS2 system is highly preferred. Experience with mobile data acquisition applications like KoboToolbox or ODK. Advanced proficiency utilizing Microsoft Office (specifically advanced spreadsheet functions in Excel).
Core Competencies: Fluent communication skills (written and spoken) in English along with regional/local operational languages. Methodical attention to detail with the ability to maintain privacy regulations surrounding data handling.

title: Programme Officer (Monitoring and Knowledge Management), NO-2, Temporary Appointment, 364 Days, #00138877 Kabul - Afghanistan, APR
description:
Afghanistan remains one of the world's most complex humanitarian and development contexts, characterized by protracted crises, recurrent natural disasters, displacement, widespread poverty, food insecurity, and significant operational and access constraints. Since August 2021, the operating environment has become increasingly challenging and dynamic, requiring UNICEF to continuously adapt its programme delivery modalities to ensure that critical services reach vulnerable children, women and families. Given the scale, complexity and risk profile of cash transfer and incentive payment programmes, UNICEF Afghanistan applies a risk-informed approach to programme monitoring and assurance. This includes routine field monitoring, third-party monitoring, post-distribution monitoring, post-payment verification, grievance redress monitoring and other quality assurance mechanisms to ensure that programmes are implemented effectively, efficiently and in accordance with UNICEF policies and agreed operational procedures.
UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.
At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.
UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.
Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.
For every child, the right to Knowledge
How can you make a difference?
Under the guidance of the supervisor, the Programme Officer (Monitoring and Knowledge Management) will provide technical and operational support to the Project Management Unit (PMU) in strengthening planning, monitoring, reporting and knowledge management for humanitarian cash transfer and incentive payment programmes. The incumbent will support the development and implementation of monitoring systems, tools and processes that generate timely, reliable and actionable information on programme performance, accountability and operational risks.
The incumbent will work closely with programme sections, field offices, implementing partners, service providers and Third-Party Monitoring Organizations (TPMOs) to support programme monitoring, third-party monitoring, post-distribution monitoring, post-payment verification, review processes and reporting requirements. The role will contribute to programme assurance, risk monitoring, organisational learning and evidence-based decision-making to strengthen programme quality, accountability and results for children and vulnerable populations.
Within the delegated authority and under the given organizational set-up, the incumbent may be assigned the primary, shared, or contributory accountabilities for all or part of the following areas of major duties and key end-results.
Key Functions, Accountabilities and related Duties/Tasks:
1. Knowledge Management for Programmes
2. Programme Development and Management
3. Programme Monitoring and Evaluations
4. Optimum Use of Program Funds
5. Rights-Based and Results-Based Programme Management Approach
6. National and Local Capacity Building/Sustainability
7. Accountability, Learning and Risk Monitoring
8. Partnership, Coordination and Collaboration.
If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: JD - Programme Officer NO-2 Kabul.pdf
To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have…
Minimum requirements:
Education: A university degree in one of the following fields is required: Monitoring and Evaluation, Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Social Sciences, Public Administration, Public Policy, Development Studies, International Development, Information Management, or another relevant technical field.
Work Experience: A minimum of two years of relevant professional work experience is required. Experience in programme monitoring, reporting, knowledge management, information management, programme planning, data analysis, monitoring and evaluation, humanitarian programming or related fields is required

Desirables:
Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) or a local language (Dari or Pashto)
Experience working with UNICEF or the United Nations system is considered an asset.

title: Disaster Risk Reduction and Early Warning Systems Specialist
company: Citizen Organization for Advocacy and Resilience, (COAR)
description:
Job Summary
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Specialist will lead and provide technical support for the planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of DRR activities in Kandahar and Helmand provinces. The position aims to strengthen community resilience to hazards by supporting risk-informed planning, preparedness, mitigation, early warning, and community-based disaster risk management in line with COAR policies and project objectives.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Primary Responsibilities
• Plan, coordinate, and implement project DRR activities in accordance with approved work plans, budgets, timelines, project objectives, and UNDP standards and require-ments.
• Support community-based disaster risk reduction initiatives, including risk aware-ness, preparedness planning, mitigation measures, and resilience-building activities.
• Conduct field visits and provide technical guidance to project teams and communi-ties to ensure quality implementation and timely resolution of challenges.
• Conduct training sessions for community members in target districts on Early Warn-ing Systems (EWS), including hazard awareness, early warning messages, communi-cation channels, and appropriate actions to take before, during, and after emergen-cies.
2. Technical Support and Expertise
• Provide technical support for the installation, configuration, testing, and operational-ization of Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) equipment and tools in the four target districts, in accordance with UNDP technical standards, specifications, and guidance.
• Coordinate with relevant technical stakeholders to ensure the proper installation, functionality, testing, and handover of MHEWS equipment, and support community members in its safe operation, basic maintenance, and use for timely early warning dissemination.
• Conduct or support hazard, vulnerability, capacity, and disaster-risk assessments in coordination with UNDP and relevant stakeholders; identify at-risk communities and priority needs.
• Support the development and implementation of community disaster risk manage-ment plans, preparedness measures, and locally appropriate risk-reduction actions, in line with project objectives.
• Contribute to early warning and early action activities, including community aware-ness, dissemination of warning information, and coordination of preparedness ac-tions.
3. Coordination and Collaboration
• Coordinate with relevant provincial and district authorities, including disaster man-agement and sectoral departments, as well as community leaders and local structures.
• Ensure effective coordination with the project donor at field, district, and provincial levels, maintain regular communication on implementation progress and operational challenges, and align project activities with agreed implementation arrangements.
• Maintain effective collaboration with COAR program, MEAL, finance, logistics, and other relevant teams to support integrated implementation and ensure compliance with UNDP project requirements.
• Engage NGOs, humanitarian actors, community-based organizations, and other stakeholders to promote information sharing, avoid duplication, and strengthen coor-dinated DRR action.
4. Monitoring and Reporting
• Collect, verify, and maintain accurate field data, activity records, benefi-ciary/community information, and supporting documentation in accordance with COAR procedures and donor reporting requirements.
• Monitor activity progress against approved plans and indicators; identify implemen-tation gaps, risks, lessons learned, and recommendations for improvement, and communicate significant issues to the line manager.
• Prepare timely and accurate field updates, activity reports, assessment findings, suc-cess stories, and other reports required by the line manager and in accordance with UNDP reporting requirements.
5. Adherence to Policies
• Comply with COAR policies, procedures, staff code of conduct, and all applicable project and donor requirements.
• Uphold safeguarding, child protection (where applicable), Prevention of Sexual Ex-ploitation and Abuse (PSEA), protection, inclusion, and do-no-harm principles in all activities.
• Ensure respectful, safe, and inclusive engagement with communities; maintain con-fidentiality and promptly report safeguarding concerns or suspected misconduct through approved channels.
6. Other Duties
• Support capacity-building sessions, community meetings, awareness campaigns, drills, and other activities relevant to the project’s DRR objectives.
• Ensure that project resources, MHEWS equipment, and materials are used responsi-bly, and that relevant installation, operation, maintenance, and handover records are properly maintained in accordance with project requirements and UNDP guidance.
• Perform other reasonable, job-related duties assigned by the line manager in line with the position’s responsibilities and project scope.

Job Requirements
QUALIFICATION AND SKILLS
• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Disaster Management, Environmental Science, Civil Engineering, Agriculture, environmental science, Development Studies, water resource management, or another relevant field. Relevant professional training in DRR, climate adaptation, and emergency preparedness is an advantage.

Mission and objectives
UNAMA was established in 2002 as a Political/ Peacebuilding Mission, exceptionally) directed and supported by the UN Department of
Peacekeeping Operations (DPKO).
Context
This mandate tasks UNAMA with the promotion and support of humanitarian assistance in line with humanitarian principles, human rights, equality for women and girls, inclusive governance, resilience, and economic stability, and with the use of our good offices for principled and constructive engagement with all national, regional, and global stakeholders in the pursuit of Afghanistan’s peace and stability.

Responsibilities
Within delegated authority and under the direct supervision of Chief FTS, the Information Systems Officer will perform the following responsibilities: • Plans and directs all major information systems projects within the mission, monitoring the progress of the systems analysis, design, development, testing and implementation of new, moderately complex systems, and/or, participates as a member of a team with responsibility for major components of the more complex systems; • Manages the budget of the Information Systems unit, formulating and monitoring budget allocations and expenditures, verifying funding and ensuring no overrun occurs; • Develops technical specifications for the procurement of equipment and contractual services, and coordinates the technical evaluation of offers and proposals received; • Develops and recommends strategies to implement global information systems projects originating out of DFS/ICTD and the mission; • Develops, implements and monitors information systems standards, guidelines and procedures; • Develops detailed systems and other functional specifications and user documentation for system as required; • Provides specialized advice to users, analysing users’ requirements and translating these into new applications; determines application systems integration and linkage issues; • Maintains, upgrades or enhances existing user systems; troubleshoots and provides continuing support, to include resolving difficult problems, advising on the use of new techniques, monitoring transactions to measure performance and continued effectiveness of assigned systems, etc; • Develops training materials, operating and user manuals; trains staff in assigned systems; • Develops disaster recovery plans relating to information systems and ensures appropriate planning and training of those responsible; • Leads the team in the operation and maintenance of internetworking systems that includes routers and switches, operating systems platforms, database management systems, servers, workstations, and related equipment; • Devises and administers disaster recovery plans; provides training for support staff to implement these plans to ensure optimal readiness; • Responsible for the proper implementation of backup and recovery procedures • Maintains a regular review of the network resources access control, data security, and server and data stores security systems; • Ensures all information security systems are properly configured and maintained • Oversees the user access control for network resources and overall network security. • Collects and analyzes data to identify trends or patterns and provides insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods to enable data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting. • Ensure that requirements and background information used for data analysis are documented. Performs other related duties as required.
Competencies
Professionalism: Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Commitment to implementing the goal of gender equality by ensuring the equal participation and full involvement of women and men in all aspects of work. Planning & Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies. Identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required. Allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work. Foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning. Monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary. Uses time efficiently. Technological Awareness: Keeps abreast of available technology. Understands applicability and limitations of technology to the work of the office. Actively seeks to apply technology to appropriate tasks. Shows willingness to learn new technology.
Education
Technical school, university and other courses and training programmes relating to the work. High school diploma or equivalent and certification/diploma in other supplemental academic qualifications, training in Information Systems is required. Information System Security Professional certification is required (CISSP). Cisco Certified Networking Professional certification is required (CCNP). Additional Industry training and certifications are desirable.
Job - Specific Qualification
Information System Security Professional certification (CISSP) is required. Cisco Certified Networking Professional certification (CCNP) is required.
Work Experience
At least ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in Information Systems and Technology, Telecommunications, or related area is required. Experience in developing ICT disaster recovery & ICT Security plans and performing related exercises is required. Experience working in a United Nations common system field operation (inclusive of peacekeeping, political missions and UN agencies, funds, and programmes) – or similar international organisation or non-governmental organisation – in a conflict or post-conflict setting is desirable. Experience in carrying out programmatic/administrative tasks necessary for the functioning of the Unit including preparation of cost estimates/budgets, reporting on budget/programme performance, and recruitment of staff is desirable.

Purpose of the Job:
The Information Management Officer will lead in coordination with sector ministries and obtain latestWASH related sector data, analysis and quality checking before dissemination to the concernedprogramme units concerned and zonal WASH teams as well as partners and external widerstakeholders. Incumbent will provide clear and concise data visualization products (e.g. maps,dashboards, infographics and financial/resource analyses) to WASH Managers, zonal teams andpartners. Incumbent will also respond to data visualization requests, including delivery of products tosupport advocacy and resource mobilization efforts of the WASH programme and WASH cluster. TheIncumbent will also lead in exchanging and dissemination of data and supporting development ofeffective methods and platforms to standardize WASH data, products and maintain good catalogueincluding maps including where possible under the GIS system. Incumbent will provide guidance to theregional WASH team and IM focal points to promote effective use of IM products for evidence-basedplanning and reporting mechanism. Incumbent also works closely with UNICEF’s PME section forharmonization of officewide planning, data management and reporting system. As a major partner ofthe WASH cluster and responsible for at least 65% of the WASH Cluster Results, having a well-managedinformation management system will significantly enhance the overall information management capacityof UNICEF and the WASH Cluster.
Key functions,accountabilities andrelated duties/tasks:
Summary of key functions/accountabilities:
1. Support to programme development and planning
2. Information Management for the WASH section
3. Programme management, monitoring and delivery of results
4. Technical and operational support to programme implementation
5. Networking and partnership building
6. Innovation, knowledge management and capacity building
1. Support to programme development and planning
- Provide evidence and data to update the situation analysis for the development, design andmanagement of WASH related programmes/projects. Research and report on development trends (e.g.economic, social, health) and data for use in programme development, management, monitoring,evaluation and delivery of results.
- Contribute to the development and establishment of sectoral programme goals, objectives, strategies,and results-based planning through research, analysis and reporting of WASH and other relatedinformation for development planning and priority and goal setting.
- Provide technical and operational support throughout all stages of programming processes byexecuting and administering a variety of technical, programme, operational, and administrativetransactions, preparing related materials and documentations, and complying with organizationalprocesses and management systems, to support programme planning, results-based planning (RBM)and monitoring and evaluating of results.
- Prepare required programme documentation, materials and data to facilitate the programme reviewand approval process.
- Support the WASH programme to improve the reporting on the RWP indicators and the SMQs andensure the capacities of the team are improved on data collection, analysis and reporting.
- Support Implementing partners on monthly reporting of achievement, clean data and submit monthsverify data based on identified indicators.
2. Information Management for the WASH section
- Develop and implement standard tools and mechanisms to enhance data management for UNICEFimplementing partners in Afghanistan.
- Consolidate all information, periodic or ad-hoc, received from the different partners and generatecomprehensive documents (including maps, dashboards, infographics and resource analyses), andpresent information in a way that is easily understood by various decision makers, ensuring the dataconfidentiality aspect.
- Support HNO, HRP process by developing Secondary Data Review (SDR), Needs severity analysis, PINand Planned reach calculation etc.
- Coordinate closely with other IMOs within UNICEF and other clusters to ensure complementarity,
harmonization and compatibility in terms of IM.
- Lead implementation of the WASH Cluster MIS in the context of Afghanistan and ensure partnerscapacity and quality improved.
- Data Collection, Compilation and Analysis.
- Participate in Inter-agency discussions including data collection, quality assurance and clearance priorto dissemination as necessary. Prepare the draft inputs reports based on collected data.
- Provide technical guidance to WASH Cluster partners on the deployment of digital innovationsincluding use of MIS and other real time data collection platforms.
- Develop the data collection tools using latest technologies to streamline the data collection process ina consistent, timely manner from partners to UNICEF and WASH Cluster.
- Build the capacity of IM/ data focal persons of partners on use of various data collection tools,reporting, analysis and IM tools.
- Contribute in generating Cross Sectoral Assessment Needs, Service Mapping, Rapid Assessments,Sitreps and Situation Analysis.
3. Programme management, monitoring and delivery of results
- Work closely and collaboratively with colleagues and partners to discuss implementation issues,provide solutions, recommendations and/or to alert appropriate officials and stakeholders for higher-level interventions and/or decisions. Keep records of reports and assessments for easy reference and/orto capture and institutionalize lessons learned.
- Participate in monitoring and evaluation exercises, programme reviews and annual sectoral reviewswith government and other counterparts to assess programmes/projects, and to report on requiredaction/interventions at the higher level of programme management.
- Monitor and report on the use of sectoral programme resources (financial, administrative and otherassets), verifying compliance with approved allocations, organizational rules, regulations, procedures anddonor commitments, standards of accountability and integrity. Report on critical issues and findings toensure timely resolution by management and stakeholders. Follow up on unresolved issues to ensureresolution.
- Prepare regular and mandated sectoral programme/project reports for management, donors andpartners to keep them informed of programme progress.
4. Technical and operational support to programme implementation
- Conduct regular programme field visits and surveys and exchange information withpartners/stakeholders to assess progress and provide technical support. Take appropriate action toresolve issues and/or refer to relevant officials for resolution. Report on critical issues, bottlenecks andpotential problems for timely action to achieve results.
- Provide technical and operational support to government counterparts, NGO partners, UN systempartners and other country office partners/donors on the application and understanding of UNICEFpolicies, strategies, processes and best practices in WASH, to support programme implementation.
5. Networking and partnership building
- Build and sustain close working partnerships with government counterparts and national stakeholdersthrough active sharing of information and knowledge to facilitate programme implementation and buildcapacity of stakeholders to achieve and sustain results on WASH.
- Participate in inter-agency meetings/events on programming to collaborate with inter-agencypartners/colleagues on UNDAF operational planning and preparation of WASH programmes/projects,and to integrate and harmonize UNICEF’s position and strategies with UNDAF development andplanning processes.
- Research information on potential donors and prepare resource mobilization materials and briefs forfund raising and partnership development purposes.
- Draft communication and information materials for CO programme advocacy to promote awareness,establish partnership/alliances and support fund raising for WASH programmes.
6. Innovation, knowledge management and capacity building
- Identify, capture, synthesize, and share lessons learned for knowledge development and to build thecapacity of stakeholders.
- Apply innovative approaches and promote good practices to support the implementation and deliveryof concrete and sustainable programme results.
- Research and report on best and cutting edge practices for development planning of knowledgeproducts and systems.
- Participate as a resource person in capacity building initiatives to enhance the competencies of clientsand stakeholders.
The Information Management Officer will enhance data accuracy, support strategic planning, strengthenadvocacy, and aid resource mobilization for WASH and support climate action through data andevidence generation. This will assure standardized data, effective visualization, and harmonization withUNICEF’s PME section, regional and zonal teams, cluster functions and the overall WASH programme,improving WASH evidence-based decision-making (including with donors and partners), acceleratingdelivery of impactful WASH interventions, strengthening WASH systems and governance, and long-termresilience for children, the communities they live in and the most vulnerable.
If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Job Description_IM Officer (WASH) NO2, FT, Kabul, Afghanistan.pdf

title: Information Management Officer (Education) (NO-2), FT, #00138039, Kabul - Afghanistan, APR (For nationals of Afghanistan only)
description:
The post holder is responsible for supporting the information management (IM) function to enable the effective functioning of the Cluster Working Group at the sub-national level, and the achievement of the core cluster functions, throughout the Humanitarian Programme Cycle (HPC) in order to facilitate a timely and effective Cluster Working Group response.The IM Officer contributes to effective coordination between sub-national and national Education Cluster coordination structures and supports information management processes related to humanitarian needs analysis, response monitoring, partner mapping, gap analysis and humanitarian reporting. The position also supports strengthened information sharing and operational alignment across humanitarian and Basic Human Needs coordination platforms within the evolving coordination architecture in Afghanistan.
UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.
At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.
UNICEF is a place where careers are built: we offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package.
Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF.
For every child, the right to Education
How can you make a difference?
Humanitarian action is of fundamental importance to UNICEF and encompasses interventions aimed at saving lives, alleviating suffering, maintaining human dignity, and protecting the rights of affected populations wherever there are humanitarian needs, as well as interventions addressing underlying risks and causes of vulnerability to disasters, fragility and conflict. UNICEF’s humanitarian action is guided by the Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian Action (CCCs) which set organizational, programmatic and operational commitments and benchmarks against which UNICEF holds itself accountable for the coverage, quality and equity of its humanitarian action and advocacy and which are mandatory for all UNICEF personnel.
Furthermore, UNICEF is committed to support humanitarian coordination through the cluster approach. Introduced as part of the humanitarian reform, the cluster approach aims at ensuring clear leadership, predictability and accountability in international responses to humanitarian emergencies by clarifying the division of labor among organizations and better defining their roles and responsibilities within the different sectors involved in the response. As a member of the IASC, UNICEF works along with national and local stakeholders (including national and local authorities, CSOs, and communities) to support humanitarian coordination and to improve the collective impact of humanitarian response. Whether the cluster approach is activated or not, UNICEF plays a key role in both global and country-level interagency coordination for its areas of programmatic responsibility. As Cluster Lead Agency (CLA) for Nutrition, WASH, Education (co-led), and Child Protection Area of Responsibility (AoR) within the Protection Cluster, UNICEF is committed to fulfil the core functions defined by the IASC when the clusters are activated or when UNICEF is asked to support sectoral coordination.
A well-run Cluster Working Group coordination team, including Information Management (IM), is a formal deliverable of the Cluster Lead Agency and forms a part of the agency’s work. The IM Officer (Education Cluster) is a core member of the Cluster Working Group coordination team.
Within the evolving humanitarian and Basic Human Needs coordination architecture in Afghanistan, the IM Officer supports information management processes that strengthen evidence-based decision-making, coordinated humanitarian response planning, inter-sectoral analysis and operational coordination between sub-national and national coordination structures.
Purpose of the Job: Under the overall direction and guidance of the Education Manager/Specialist Cluster Coordinator, the IM Officer (Education Cluster) manages and supports the information management function of the Education Cluster Working Group at sub-national level. The incumbent supports the collection, analysis, management and dissemination of information required to enable evidence-based humanitarian planning, response coordination, monitoring and reporting.
The postholder's main tasks and responsibilities will include but not be limited to:
Coordination and Representation
As a member of the coordination team, contribute to the effective roll out and monitoring of the core cluster functions (as outlined by the IASC Reference Module) and to the Humanitarian Programme Cycle (HNO, HRP and CCPM),
Support the Cluster Working Group IM function and coordinate with others within the function to ensure effective communication, reporting and engagement,
Actively engage with other IMs through relevant IMWGs, including participating in the Cluster Working Group IMWG and representing the Cluster Working Group on the inter-cluster IMWG as relevant at sub-national level,
Promote harmonized and coordinated approaches to IM across partners, AoRs/ Clusters Working Groups and OCHA at sub-national level.
IM Function Support
Implement an IM strategy and data collection and analysis plan at sub-national level that take into account the information needs of stakeholders and that are compliant with standards and protocols for ethical data and information management and that is aligned with the national level IM strategy and plan,
Implement regular secondary data reviews and primary data collection including designing questionnaires using appropriate tools,
Conduct data processing including organizing, cleaning, triangulating, evaluating and validating the data,
Analyze data to meet identified information needs of sub-national Cluster Working Group members and other stakeholders,
Create accurate, quality and timely information products that are in line with agreed style guides,
Disseminate information and information products through appropriate channels,
Maintain and ensure the accessibility of a common and shared secure storage system,
Gather feedback on IM products and use them to make improvements.
Needs Assessment and Analysis
Working collaboratively with other members of the Cluster Working Group at national and sub-national level, contribute to the planning and implementation of needs assessment and analysis, including joint assessments and analysis, as requested,
Collect information on economic needs, markets and price monitoring to support the equal consideration and use of all programme delivery modalities (in-kind, cash, voucher and services) as relevant at sub-national level,
Work with sub-national Cluster Working Group participants to identify information gaps, agree and implement ways to bridge those gaps by providing technical support to partners,
Analyze needs assessment data to provide required information for the HNO including estimating People in Need (PIN),
Contribute to joint and inter-sectoral analysis processes and support alignment of needs analysis findings across clusters/sectors and relevant humanitarian and Basic Human Needs coordination platforms at sub-national level.
Strategic Response Planning
Implement partner presence mapping at sub-national level,
Contribute to strategic planning, response prioritization and development of humanitarian response plans and related analytical products, including support to objectives, indicators, targets, partner mapping and response monitoring.
Resource Mobilization
Monitor and analyze the sub-national Cluster Working Group’s financial situation and support financial tracking,
Support and advocate with Cluster Working Group partners for financial reporting on the Financial Tracking Service (FTS),
Support evidence-based advocacy and resource mobilization by providing accurate, relevant and timely data, information and information products.
Implementation and Monitoring
Implement and maintain a sub-national Cluster Working Group monitoring plan and associated databases, including a response monitoring (3/4/5Ws) database that is in line with and contributes to national level databases,
Ensure the sub-national Cluster Working Group monitoring plan, and 3/4/5Ws include programme delivery modalities (in-kind, cash, voucher and services),
Support sub-national Cluster Working Group members to contribute timely and quality periodic monitoring reports on Cluster Working Group and OCHA platforms,
Support monitoring in the areas of information flows, dissemination, processing, analysis and dissemination,
Contribute to quantitative and qualitative gaps and coverage analysis to identify spatial and temporal gaps, overlaps and coverage of the sub-national Cluster Working Group humanitarian response,
Monitor adherence to relevant sector quality standards, regulations and codes at sub-national level.
Operational Peer Review and Evaluation
Participate in the annual cluster coordination performance monitoring (CCPM) exercise and annual review,
Contribute to sectoral and broader humanitarian evaluations.
Accountability to Affected People
Be accountable to affected populations by encouraging the meaningful participation of affected people, maintaining an effective feedback mechanism and handling complaints appropriately, by ensuring data about the most vulnerable is systematically collected and analysed, and by encouraging partners to work accountably,
Ensure the inclusion of cross cutting issues (age, child protection, disability, gender, gender, gender-based violence (GBV) mitigation and response and HIV & AIDS) in Cluster Working Group data collection, analysis and dissemination,
Adhere to child safeguarding and PSEA policies including procedures for challenging and reporting incidents.
Strengthen National and Local Capacity
Support or implement actions to strengthen local and national leadership and capacity by encouraging participation of local and national actors in the IM activities of the sub-national Cluster Working Group and providing support to partners to overcome technical and operational challenges in participating in IM activities,
Implement an IM capacity assessment and capacity development plan for sub-national Cluster Working Group partners.
The IM Officer (Education Cluster) position is based in Afghanistan and supports the Education Cluster coordination function at sub-national or regional level. The position reports to the Education Manager/Specialist Cluster Coordinator (P3/P4) and supports information management, data analysis, reporting and coordination processes required for effective Education Cluster coordination and humanitarian response planning.
If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Information Management Officer, NO2, Job Description.pdf
To qualify an advocate for every child you will have…
Minimum requirements:
Education: Bachelor or equivalent (First Level University Degree) in Information Management, Information Systems, Info. Technology, Computer Science, Statistics, Science, information management, information systems, geographic information systems, information technology, computer science, statistics, social sciences, data science and any other related field is required.
Work Experience: 2 years of relevant work experience in Information Technology, Humanitarian Assistance, Education, Emergency, Monitoring and Evaluation, Response, information management, humanitarian coordination, education in emergencies, data analysis, needs assessment, monitoring and reporting, geospatial analysis, data visualization, response planning, cluster coordination and any other related field is a requirement.

Humanitarian coordination experience, cluster IM training, INEE minimum standards, Sphere standards, Core Humanitarian Standard experience will be an asset.
Relevant experience at country level, particularly in development, fragile settings and humanitarian contexts will be considered an asset.

title: Full Stack Developer
description:
Role Summary
The Full Stack Developer is responsible for designing, developing, integrating, deploying, and supporting MOAM’s web, backend, and mobile applications. The role requires strong hands-on experience with .NET Core backend development and microservice architecture, Next.js frontend development, Flutter mobile development, and the infrastructure required to run these systems reliably in production.
The position will contribute to the design, development, and evolution of MOAM’s digital logistics ecosystem, including Courier and Cargo products across web and mobile platforms, shared backend services, system integrations, and future digital solutions, with responsibility spanning APIs, distributed services, caching, messaging, observability, databases, containerization, server administration, security, performance, and third-party integrations. The developer is expected to work across the complete software delivery lifecycle and collaborate closely with the Technology Unit and business stakeholders.

Duties and Responsibilities
A. Backend Development & Microservices
· Design, develop, maintain, and optimize backend services and REST APIs using C# and ASP.NET Core / .NET Core.
· Design services using microservice architecture, clear service boundaries, maintainable domain/application layers, and clean architecture principles.
· Implement authentication, authorization, role/permission management, API validation, error handling, background processing, and secure service-to-service communication.
· Work with SQL Server and relational data access using Entity Framework Core; design efficient schemas, migrations, indexes, transactions, and queries.
· Implement distributed caching and cache invalidation strategies using Redis or equivalent technologies.
· Use RabbitMQ for asynchronous messaging, event-driven workflows, queues, retries, and reliable communication between services; implement real-time application features using appropriate technologies such as SignalR/WebSockets where required.
· Integrate MOAM systems with ERP (including Sage), CRM, payment gateways, SMS/notification services, Firebase, customs systems, and other internal or third-party platforms.
B. Frontend Development
· Develop and maintain responsive, secure, production-ready web applications using Next.js, React, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.
· Integrate frontend applications with backend APIs, authentication flows, real-time features, and server-side/client-side data fetching as appropriate.
· Build reusable UI components, handle application state effectively, and ensure performance, accessibility, maintainability, and cross-browser compatibility.
C. Mobile Application Development
· Develop, maintain, and troubleshoot cross-platform mobile applications using Flutter and Dart.
· Integrate Flutter applications with .NET APIs and Firebase services such as Cloud Messaging/push notifications, authentication, analytics, or other required Firebase capabilities.
· Manage mobile application state, API communication, error handling, local persistence, release builds, and application performance.
D. DevOps, Server & Deployment Management
· Containerize applications and supporting services using Docker and Docker Compose; maintain reliable environment configuration across development, staging, and production.
· Administer and troubleshoot application servers, preferably Linux-based environments, including services, networking, ports, SSL/TLS certificates, reverse proxies such as Nginx, storage, permissions, and resource usage.
· Support CI/CD pipelines, source control workflows, environment variables/secrets, deployment automation, backups, rollback procedures, and production releases.
· Monitor application and infrastructure health and diagnose production issues across services, containers, databases, logs, queues, caches, and network dependencies.
E. Logging, Monitoring & Reliability
· Implement structured application logging using Serilog and centralized log monitoring/analysis using Seq.
· Design meaningful logs, correlation identifiers, health checks, metrics, alerts, and diagnostics to support distributed systems and production troubleshooting.
· Improve application performance, scalability, resilience, fault handling, and availability through profiling, testing, and operational monitoring.
F. Quality, Security & Engineering Practices
· Write unit and integration tests and perform API, frontend, and mobile validation before release.
· Apply secure coding practices for authentication, authorization, secrets, data protection, input validation, dependency management, and API security.
· Participate in technical design, sprint planning, backlog refinement, code reviews, Git workflows, troubleshooting, and documentation.
· Produce clear technical documentation for architecture, APIs, deployments, integrations, and operational procedures.

Job Requirements
· Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a closely related field, or equivalent demonstrable professional experience.
· Strong professional experience building full-stack production applications, with .NET Core / ASP.NET Core as the primary backend technology.
· Hands-on experience with microservices, REST APIs, SQL Server, Entity Framework Core, Redis caching, RabbitMQ messaging, Serilog, and Seq.
· Hands-on experience with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and modern frontend development practices.
· Hands-on experience developing mobile applications with Flutter/Dart and integrating Firebase services.
· Practical experience with Docker/containerization, Git, server administration, application deployment, and production troubleshooting.
· Good understanding of software architecture, security, performance, scalability, concurrency, testing, and distributed-system fundamentals.
· Ability to independently analyze technical problems, communicate clearly, document solutions, and collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
· Good command of English for technical documentation and communication; Dari and/or Pashto are advantageous.
Preferred / Advantageous Experience
· API gateways/reverse proxies (for example YARP or Nginx), CQRS/Mediator patterns, background workers, scheduled jobs, and distributed tracing.
· CI/CD platforms, cloud or VPS environments, DNS/SSL management, backups, monitoring, and production incident response.
· Experience integrating ERP/CRM, logistics, warehouse, cargo, payment, notification, or other enterprise systems.
· Experience with Swagger/OpenAPI, Postman, automated testing, code quality tools, and Agile/Scrum delivery.

All documents should be submitted in PDF format , with the file name clearly indicating your first and last name and the position applied for . Please note that interviews may be conducted while the position remains open and under announcement .

title: Abuse Research Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote from the US
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.
What you’ll do
As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence. Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains. Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.
Responsibilities
Proactive Threat Hunting & Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data.
FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints.
Threat Intelligence & Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows.
Cross-Functional Advisories & Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security.
Agentic Testing & Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls.
Who you are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
5+ years of experience conducting threat intelligence, threat hunting, or technical incident response within cyber security, product abuse, or trust domains.
5+ years of experience analyzing large, complex datasets using data analytics tools to identify anomalies, map behavioral trends, and solve complex fraud problems.
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with demonstrated experience using code and scripting to automate workflows, build investigative tools, or query big data pipelines.

We run security the way the best engineering-led companies do:
Security reduces toil. Our job is to make the rest of the company faster and safer at the same time. If a control adds friction without reducing risk, it is a defect.
Paved paths, safe by default. We invest in guardrails, golden paths, and secure-by-default infrastructure so the easy choice is the secure choice. We prefer preventing classes of problems over chasing individual findings.
Partnership over gatekeeping. Security succeeds only through deep collaboration with engineering, IT, and business teams. We embed with builders, we ship alongside them, and we take on their constraints as our own.
Engineering-grade rigor. We treat security problems as engineering problems: automated, measurable, code-reviewed, and continuously improved.

title: Product Engineer (PM)
description:
Location: Fully Remote
Compensation: $23.08 to $34.62 USD/hour
Benefits: 15 days PTO. Christmas Day and New Year's Day paid off.
Fair warning: the pace is intense and the ambiguity is real. But you'll feel yourself growing every single week, even the rough ones, and you'll be doing it next to people who actually celebrate your wins and have your back.
We're the all-in-one agentic marketing platform. AI-native from day one. We're not joining a category, we're defining it.
We're looking for a Product Engineer to own a pod's output end-to-end: strategy, specs, QA, and enough technical depth to unblock engineers or write the code yourself when that's the fastest path forward. If you want real ownership, move fast, and raise the bar every week, keep reading. If you've been waiting for a PM role that doesn't ask you to leave your technical background at the door, this is it.
What you'll own
Own the roadmap for your pod: define what gets built, kill low-leverage work, and protect your engineers' time and focus
Write specs that start with the problem, not the solution, and ship every brief with a clear success criterion
Participate technically: read the codebase, debug independently, and ship small things when it's faster than context-switching an engineer
Own QA end-to-end: test plans, regression passes, release sign-off, and post-deploy monitoring in Sentry and Grafana
Keep the pod moving: fast decisions, async-first communication, and zero ambiguity about what's next
Close the feedback loop between customers, data, and product direction, and hold yourself accountable to the KPIs you define
You'll thrive here if...
You've shipped production code before and you're honest with yourself about your technical depth
You treat a spec as a hypothesis to pressure-test, not a document to execute against
You don't wait to be told what to do. You see the gap and you move.
Deadlines don't rattle you. Ambiguity doesn't either.
You're an AI power user, not someone who's "open to learning it someday."
You communicate clearly, especially when things are unclear.
You have opinions and you're not afraid to bring them.
You can laugh at a chaotic week on Friday and mean it.
What we're looking for
3+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS, startup or high-growth environment
A hands-on technical background: production code, a bootcamp, or demonstrable ability to navigate a full-stack codebase
Comfortable reading Python and JavaScript/TypeScript; able to write SQL, reason about REST contracts, and follow frontend state
Proven QA ownership: test cases, regression cycles, structured bug reports, release sign-off
Daily fluency with Claude Code or equivalent. Not "open to it." Actually using it.
Strong written communication. Your specs are clear and complete on the first read.
Available in EST
What working here actually looks like
High expectations. Real ownership. Things change fast and we don't apologize for it. You'll work with smart people who push you, a product that keeps getting better, and a team that's genuinely building something new.
The boundary between product and engineering is intentionally blurred here. The best product decisions are inseparable from technical reality, and we hire people who understand that.
We'll probably give you more to own than you expected. That's on purpose.
We use AI every day, across every function. That's just how we work.
What we stand for
We are obsessed with our customers, and making them obsessed with us
We figure it the f**k out
We go to war on our problems quickly
We are strategic. We work smart, not just hard.
We're fun AF
About Search Atlas
Search Atlas helps marketing teams move faster, make smarter decisions, and do more with less. We're a $30M+ ARR company, 215 people, bootstrapped, and building the infrastructure for the next era of marketing. No outside funding. No fluff. Just product.

Vercel is the agentic infrastructure company, freeing people and agents to ship what's next. For more than a decade we've helped builders move from idea to production with speed, security, and exceptional developer experience.

We're looking for a Staff level Engineer to lead the design and development of a next-generation Data Platform at Vercel. This is a unique opportunity to architect a foundational system that will power data across our products and business, supporting everything from real-time analytics to AI/ML initiatives.
Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Data Engineering, you'll define the technical vision for our data ecosystem, work across the organization to align engineering strategy with product goals, and build scalable, reliable systems using modern technologies like Kafka, ClickHouse, Tinybird, and Snowflake.

Collaborate with data scientists and machine learning teams to evolve infrastructure that supports advanced analytics and AI initiatives, serving as a key contributor to strategy, tooling, and platform enhancements for ML-related workloads.
Act as a key decision-maker for discovering, vetting, and selecting data architectures and technologies critical to Vercel's success, and establish multi-phase strategic roadmaps that align with overall business objectives and drive data platform maturity.

8+ years of experience in data engineering, data architecture, or related roles, with at least 5 years at the Principal Engineer level.

About the Role:
An AI Experience Engineer owns the full lifecycle of the journeys our customers have with Upgrade's AI agent on chat, voice and email: creation, optimization, edge case handling and containment growth. They build journeys in Sierra's no-code tooling, partner with Upgrade's product groups to bring their servicing flows to the agent, and are accountable for whether the agent resolves the customer's issue safely, accurately and without a human.
We are hiring an AI Experience Engineer to own Upgrade's customer-facing AI agent. You will sit between engineering, product and customer operations. You will turn servicing workflows, such as making a payment, checking loan details, updating an address or enabling autopay, into production journeys and keep improving them after launch. You will build and own the journeys end to end, from first draft to steady state. The work is part builder, part analyst: design the flow, handle the edge cases, read the transcripts, and keep raising containment. Containment, CSAT, transfer quality and hallucination rate are your metrics.
Within your first year, you will own a portfolio of journeys across products (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, HELOC, Deposits) and help set the standards for how Upgrade builds, tests and ships AI experiences.
Our Core Technologies
Sierra Agent Studio (no-code journeys), Sierra simulations and conversation analytics, GraphQL and REST APIs (as journey tools), Genesys (contact center handoff), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, Javascript/Typescript, Claude and other LLM tools.
What You'll Do
• Journey creation: Design and build Sierra journeys in Agent Studio for chat, voice and email, from discovery with operations through production rollout
• Optimization: Review transcripts, recordings and analytics every week, find where conversations fail or transfer, and ship fixes to journey logic, instructions and knowledge
• Edge case handling: Map the unhappy paths (failed payments, mismatched identity, delinquent accounts, unsupported requests) and make sure each ends in a correct answer or a clean handoff
• Containment: Own containment and CSAT targets per journey, run staged rollouts (1% → 100%), and prioritize the work that moves those numbers most
• Product partnership: Work with product groups (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, Deposits) to scope new journeys, keep journeys current as products change, and define the APIs the agent needs
• Safety and compliance: Apply tiered authentication and step-up verification, verbatim compliance language and guardrails against hallucination and off-policy answers
• Handoffs: Design transfers to human agents in Genesys with accurate summaries and auth context
• Testing: Build simulation and regression suites so every journey change ships with evidence it did not break existing behavior
• Monitoring: Watch latency, errors and drop-offs in SumoLogic and Grafana, and own the alerts
• Voice tuning: Latency, filler phrases, interruptions, personality and tone
• Sierra relationship: Be the technical owner on our side, escalate platform issues and shape roadmap asks
What We Look For:
• 3–5 years of Frontend Software Engineering experience, or equivalent experience in Solutions Engineering, Conversational AI or Technical Product roles
• Working knowledge of how LLM agents behave: instructions, tool calls, knowledge retrieval, and where each one fails
• Experience building evaluations for non-deterministic systems: test sets, simulations, LLM-as-judge, regression gates
• Enough technical depth to read API specs, work with backend engineers on REST and GraphQL integrations, and reason about authorization and permission scopes
• Working knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript, with the ability to build and maintain coded journeys and integrate APIs within conversational AI platforms.

description:

URL: https://www.askablelabs.com/
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.
You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.
Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.
How it works
Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.
Requirements
2+ years of professional software engineering
Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
Regular use of an AI coding tool
Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
At least 10 hours a week, starting now

Nice to have
Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
Experience building agent tasks or RL environments
Terms
US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us

Identify gaps in HMIS utilization and recommend practical measures to improve system use and operational efficiency.

Ability to prepare basic technical records and support the generation of HMIS reports.

Communication, coordination, and teamwork.

title: Consultant for the Development of the Campaign Information Management System (CI
description:
IMPORTANT – APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS
Please read the “How to Apply” section carefully before submitting your application. A Technical Proposal and a Financial Proposal are required for your application to be considered. Applications submitted without both required proposals may not be considered.
Our Vision & Mission
We envision a world in which all people have access to high quality and enduring solutions to improve and maintain their health and well-being. MCD aspires to be a premier partner of choice and an internationally recognized leader, innovator, and trusted partner in applied, cross-national public health solutions. Our mission is to improve the health and well-being of people worldwide through enduring, high-quality, cost-effective, and universally accessible public health solutions.
About the Position
The Bioko Island Malaria Elimination Project (BIMEP) is a 22 year partnership between the Government of Equatorial Guinea, oil sector partners and MCD Global Health , working toward malaria elimination under the Vice President's Vision 2030 strategy. The Ministry of Health leads the effort through the National Malaria Control Program, and MCD Global Health serves as implementing partner and operational coordinator. The 2026 to 2030 phase extends program activities from Bioko Island to mainland Equatorial Guinea and Annobón Island.
The Campaign Information Management System (CIMS) is a proprietary MCD platform that holds the programmatic data for BIMEP field interventions, including indoor residual spraying (IRS), MILD distribution, larval source management and malaria indicator surveys. It is the data backbone of the spatial decision support system that plans and directs field interventions in Equatorial Guinea, combining geographic information with field data reported during each campaign so that managers can monitor coverage and redirect teams while activities are under way.
PALU carries out MCD's analytical work across MCD’s international program. Its processes include automated reports, data models built with dbt, and scheduled extraction of data from external sources such as DHIS2. These processes developed over several years on different servers and tools. With fewer systems now in use, MCD intends to consolidate them on a smaller, documented and less costly architecture built on GitLab for version control and continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD), AWS for hosting, and possibly Databricks as a unified data warehouse.
MCD seeks a consultant to carry out this consolidation through three deliverable areas, and to provide maintenance and technical support for the systems as they are put in place. The consultant will work within the existing team under the technical direction of the Digital Health Tools and Systems Lead. The work should leave PALU and digital health staff able to operate, modify and extend these systems without outside help.
This consultancy is a two-month pilot running from November to December 2026, aligned with MCD's budget year. It tests the working arrangement and the fit between the consultant, the tools and the team. If the pilot goes well, MCD expects to extend the engagement in 2027 for further CIMS development and continued maintenance.
Requirements
Key Responsibilities
Databricks Assessment and Pilot
Assess Databricks against PALU's current and expected data warehouse needs and against the requirements of active projects, including comparison with the PostgreSQL environment MCD already runs on AWS.
Set up and configure a small data model in Databricks, using a representative subset of PALU data, to estimate compute, storage and licensing costs under realistic use.
Configure connectors to the priority external data sources agreed with PALU, to test how a data warehouse would be populated and kept current.
Prepare a cost benefit analysis for MCD PALU covering direct costs, staff time, skills required, and the risks of adopting and of not adopting the platform.

Bei DACHS IT sollst du nicht einfach nur „eine Stelle“ haben, sondern ein Arbeitsumfeld, das zu deinem Leben, deinen Stärken und deinen Zielen passt. Deshalb bieten wir dir:

Gemeinsam finden wir Projekte, die zu deinem Profil und deiner Entwicklung passen – z. B. Plattformaufbau, Cloud-Migration, Automatisierung, Operations oder technische Schulungen bei Kund:innen.

Wir setzen nicht auf jährliche Pflichttermine, sondern auf regelmäßige, ehrliche Gespräche auf Augenhöhe – du gibst uns Feedback, wir dir. So wissen wir alle, woran wir sind, und können unsere gemeinsamen nächsten Entwicklungsschritte gezielt unterstützen.

wen suchen wir?
Wir suchen ein Teammitglied, das unsere Kunden im direkten Kontakt berät, gemeinsam mit ihnen bedarfsorientierte Lösungen entwickelt und sie bei der Umsetzung unterstützt. title: Principal Linux Security Engineer
description:
CIQ OVERVIEW
CIQ builds the enterprise infrastructure that powers the world's most demanding workloads. From the operating system layer through AI infrastructure, high-performance computing, and cloud-native orchestration, CIQ delivers the speed, security, scalability, and sovereignty that major enterprises, government agencies, and research institutions depend on.
CIQ is the founding support and services partner of Rocky Linux and the developer of the RLC Pro family of Enterprise Linux distributions, Fuzzball workload orchestration, Warewulf Pro cluster provisioning, and Ascender Pro automation. Our customers include some of the largest and most technically sophisticated organizations in the world, working across HPC, AI/ML, defense, and regulated industries.
We are a company of builders, operators, and open source practitioners. If you want to do work that matters, at a company that is genuinely changing how enterprise infrastructure gets built and run, we want to talk.
POSITION SUMMARY
This isn't a traditional job description. It describes the specific person we're looking for: an engineer who understands the Linux operating system from a security perspective.
What does that mean in practice? Here is what we need from this role:
How security errata works in an operating system (CSAF, VEX, Advisories) and how to create them and use them in various aspects of the systems, from updateinfo in repos to a security feed for security scanners to ingest.
Compliance on an operating system - Building out STIG and DIS profiles. Understanding how to improve OpenSCAP and building Ansible scripts to apply the security profiles, not just applying scripts that someone else built.
Proactive security in an operating system, like build flags, LKRG, SELinux. How to really secure the OS in a way that also allows it to be usable. Not hooking it up to the internet is not an acceptable security answer.
How to build tools to make the above happen faster and interact with AI to speed up development, testing, and release.
CVE scoring - How they are scored and what that means. It doesn’t mean that you know how to look up a score in NIST, but it means you have used the CVSS calculator and you know why it is scored a 7.8 vs. a 5.5
CVE affectedness - You understand how to determine if a piece of software is affected by a CVE and how different aspects of build and configuration change the affectedness.
Is This Role Right for You?
If the requirements above don't resonate with your experience, this position is likely not the right fit. If you meet most of them, we'd like to hear from you. We're looking for candidates who are genuinely engaged with this work, so we ask that automated or mass applications be avoided.
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
Proven work experience in Security and/or Linux Engineering with a focus on the Linux OS.
At least 4 years of experience doing security in Linux and at least 2 years of experience building Linux Packages
BENEFITS
Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
Flexible paid time off.
Employee stock options.
Remote work; no travel required for most positions.
